# The Rethink Matters tag system (draft v1)

*Generated by `build/build.py` from `curation/meta.yaml` and `curation/tags.yaml`; the counts are live (2026-10-16).*

## The idea in one paragraph

Every discussion prompt on the map carries two kinds of tag. **Lenses** say *where a prompt sits*: its length scale, the working group that would carry it, which pillar of the mission it advances, which of the World Economic Forum's four values it speaks to. **Semantic tags** say *what it is about* and, more importantly, *why it belongs with other prompts*: the tension it sits on, the concept at work, the barrier in the way, the material or setting, the method. Two prompts that share a semantic tag are linked however far apart their themes are. That is the network effect: a connection between ‘Chronic bioelectrodes’ (medicine) and ‘Hype vs evidence’ (commercial value) comes from a shared tag, rather than from someone having to spot it.

## Five design rules, and how the vocabulary scores

1. **Cross-cutting, not a re-labelled theme.** A tag must be able to connect at least two themes. *Result:* 53 of 53 tags span two or more themes (median 3, maximum 6).
2. **Reusable, but not ubiquitous.** Aim for roughly 3–14 prompts per tag: rarer tags create no network, commoner ones create a hairball. *Result:* min 3, median 5, max 14 prompts per tag; 5.4 semantic tags per prompt.
3. **Faceted.** Five orthogonal families of tag, so two prompts can be linked for different reasons. Open a tag on the map to see everything it ties together.
4. **A tag is a reason.** Each tag has a one-line definition of what linking two notes by it *means*; tensions have two named poles.
5. **Your own language first.** Scale (micro/meso/macro), working groups (WG1–3), the mission pillars (the site tagline) and the WEF values come from your sheets, your site and the central report. Only the semantic tags are new, and they were derived by reading every provocation and note.

## What the resulting network looks like

| measure | value |
|---|---|
| prompts / themes / discussions | 60 / 9 / 43 (18 with notes) |
| semantic tags in use | 53 |
| hand-written bridges (with a one-line reason) | 73 |
| links shown by default (bridges + strong shared-tag links) | 105 |
| share of default links that cross a theme boundary | 63% |
| connected components among prompts (default links) | 1 (the largest covers 60 of 60) |
| average hops between two prompts | 3.8 |

**Tags that bridge the most themes** (the best ‘connectors’): Definitions & shared language (6 themes, 12 prompts); Sensing, repair & adaptation (6 themes, 9 prompts); Engineered cells & hosts (6 themes, 8 prompts); Medical & clinical (5 themes, 13 prompts); Regulation & long-term evidence (5 themes, 12 prompts); Proteins & peptides (5 themes, 10 prompts); Modelling & AI (5 themes, 10 prompts); General & portable ↔ specific & contextual (5 themes, 9 prompts).

## Layer 2: semantic tags

### Tensions: *What is being pulled in two directions?*

The debates the group keeps returning to. A topic carries a tension tag when it sits on that fault line; two notes on the same fault line are in conversation even if they are about different materials.

| tag | meaning | prompts | themes | for example |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| `tension/general-vs-specific` **General & portable ↔ specific & contextual** | Abstraction and standardisation versus context-specific precision: in principles, signals, standards, models and platforms. | 9 | 5 | Classifying materials; DNA is fancy PEG; Portable design principles |
| `tension/near-vs-far` **Near-term utility ↔ long-term & speculative** | Market-ready use versus early-stage, blue-sky or speculative research and futures. | 8 | 4 | Classifying materials; Unexplored biological features; Patterning to organs |
| `tension/private-vs-common` **Private ownership ↔ common good** | Who owns, funds and benefits: IP, markets, commons, public data, shared facilities, consumer protection. | 7 | 4 | Public datasets; Who captures value; Funding platform medicines |
| `tension/copy-vs-principles` **Copy nature's parts ↔ extract its rules** | Whether to reproduce biological structures or abstract the principles behind them, and whether those principles are portable, and precise enough to design with. | 6 | 2 | Portable design principles; Gradients as design; Engineering a tree |
| `tension/hype-vs-evidence` **Breakthrough hype ↔ premature dismissal** | Telling genuine progress from hype (and from reflexive dismissal) when evidence is incomplete: in claims, benchmarks, ventures and long-term data. | 4 | 3 | AI meets biological constraints; Lessons from ventures; Hype vs evidence |
| `tension/niche-vs-bulk` **High-value niche ↔ bulk volume** | Micro-scale, high-value uses versus commodity-scale production, and how energy, cost and infrastructure tip the balance. | 4 | 2 | Micro vs bulk; Cellulose, wood & concrete; Energy, cost & fit |
| `tension/access-vs-safety` **Open access ↔ safety & misuse** | Widening access to tools and devices (convivial, at-home, consumer) versus managing risk, misuse, accountability and regulation. | 4 | 2 | Infection-sensing dressings; Who benefits? Wounds & clinicians; Care & convivial tech |
| `tension/living-vs-inert` **Living & maintained ↔ inert & finished** | Materials that stay alive and need care versus ones that were alive, or are fabricated and finished; and what that means for definition, durability and end of life. | 4 | 2 | Living vs formerly living; Material 'intelligence'; Hydrated materials |
| `tension/platform-vs-bespoke` **Derisk once & reuse ↔ approve case by case** | Whether a validated platform can be reused across products or indications, or each application needs its own evidence and approval. | 4 | 2 | Standardising dynamic properties; Funding platform medicines; Derisk once: gene delivery |
| `tension/control-vs-emergence` **Imposed control ↔ self-assembly & emergence** | How much to specify with machines (printing, patterning) versus letting living or soft matter organise itself, and what we are optimising for. | 3 | 2 | World models & inverse design; Patterning to organs; Printing meets growth |
| `tension/robust-vs-adaptable` **Robust & uniform ↔ adaptive & variable** | Designing for reliable, uniform outcomes versus tolerating or exploiting variability: in tissues, feedstocks, bioprocesses and materials in service. | 3 | 3 | Signalling & crosstalk; Variable feedstocks; Survive use, degrade after |
| `tension/replace-vs-reinvent` **Drop-in replacement ↔ new capability** | Whether biobased materials should match incumbents on the incumbents' terms, or win by offering functions incumbents cannot (sensing, repair, adaptation, locality). | 3 | 2 | Engineering a tree; Replace or reinvent; Cellulose, wood & concrete |

| `tension/natural-vs-good` **Biological origin ↔ demonstrated benefit** | 'Bio' describes origin or process, not performance: it does not by itself imply safety, biodegradability, sustainability or ethical value. | 3 | 3 | Biobased vs biomaterial; Lessons from ventures; 'Bio' ≠ good |
| `tension/human-vs-organism` **Human benefit ↔ duties to other life** | What we owe the organisms and ecosystems we use, engineer or affect: not just through them, but to them. | 3 | 2 | Duties to organisms; Salt tolerance & ecosystems; When to let materials die |

## How to tag a new provocation (five questions)

1. **Scale:** at what length scale does the problem become visible: micro, meso or macro (pick the one where it is most visible; add a second only if it is truly both)?
2. **Pillar and value:** which pillar of the mission does it advance (design, climate, governance, translation), and does it speak to equity, humility, sustainability or solidarity? Leave *value* empty if none fits.
3. **Tension:** what is being pulled in two directions? If you can name both poles, use or add a `tension/…` tag.
4. **Barrier and concept:** what stands in the way, and which phenomenon or principle is at work?
5. **Domain and method:** which material system or setting, and which tool? Then add one or two hand-written bridges to prompts it echoes, opposes, enables or builds on, each with a one-line reason.

Aim for **4–8 semantic tags** per prompt. Before inventing a tag, check whether an existing one fits; a new tag earns its place only if it would sit on at least three prompts across at least two themes.

## How tags turn into links

For every pair of prompts the build adds up the weight of the semantic tags they share (rarer tags weigh more, `ln((N+1)/(n+1))`; tensions count 1.5×, domains 0.7×, methods 0.8×) and adds 2.5 for each discussion they both grew from. Pairs scoring at least `DEFAULT_MIN` (6.0, set in `build/build.py`) are drawn on the Regime and the Niche, and listed in each prompt's note. Hand-written bridges are always shown. Lenses are *not* used for linking (every prompt has a scale, so sharing one means little).

## Things to decide

* **Pillar, value and every semantic tag are the map author's first draft.** Scale and working group come from your sheets where recorded.
* The nine themes in the sheet include **Theme 9 (ocean & extreme environments)**; the brief mentioned eight. All nine are on the map.
* The *value* lens uses the four values from the WEF report behind the central question. If you would rather use the ten shared aims on your About page, the facet can be swapped without touching anything else.
